title: Micro-Optimizing the Idle/Wait Loop (Amdahl's Law Violation)
pattern: Spending engineering effort optimizing a code routine or component that consumes less than 1% of the application's runtime or executing during system idle time.
why_bad: According to Amdahl's Law, even a 10x speedup of a routine that represents 1% of runtime improves overall application performance by less than 0.1%. Micro-optimizing idle routines is a complete waste of development effort and compromises readability [296, 337, 340].
detection: Tuning loops, allocations, or math expressions inside utility functions, debug logs, or shutdown sequences that are rarely called or run during idle periods.
counterexample: Hard real-time systems where the absolute worst-case latency must be minimized. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Profile the application using a CPU sampler first, and focus optimization efforts exclusively on the highest-priority hot paths (> 10% of runtime).
